I am a mother of two children and a patient who is currently waiting for surgery. I live with severe, ongoing pain that often prevents me from sleeping at night and significantly limits my daily functioning. Because of my medical condition, travelling long distances to access healthcare has been extremely difficult.

I remained registered with this GP surgery only because it was close to my home, not because of the quality of care. I had no realistic alternative while unwell. Despite my serious health condition and vulnerability, I was repeatedly treated with lack of compassion, dismissiveness, and unprofessional behaviour.

In particular, the way I was spoken to by reception staff over the phone was distressing and unacceptable. Calls were handled in a manner that made me feel dismissed rather than supported. As a patient in severe pain and awaiting surgery, I should never have been spoken to in this way. This is not a single misunderstanding but a pattern of behaviour that caused significant emotional harm and left me feeling broken at a time when I needed medical care the most.

The NHS funds this GP surgery, and therefore has a responsibility to ensure that patients are treated with dignity, respect, and basic human decency. I am formally calling for the NHS to take action by:
•	Reviewing how this surgery operates
•	Investigating how reception staff and clinicians communicate with patients
•	Checking phone call handling, recordings, and patient records
•	Holding the GP surgery accountable for staff conduct and training
